explanation: The senior officer who supervises administration across a division, which includes several districts.
The senior officer responsible for the administration of a district.
An officer who manages and supervises administration in an assigned subdivision or taluka area.
A revenue officer in Sindh who deals with taluka-level land records and revenue administration.

A field-level revenue official also known as village staff, who deals with Deh Level land Records and Revenue Administration, also collect, Land Revenue, Land Tax, Water Cess and other tax applicable in the law.
A government officer authorised under Sindh Land Revenue, Act, 1967 to perform revenue functions, such as maintaining land records or handling revenue matters.
BOR also known as Secretariat of Revenue Department to Provincial Government, and mother institution of all revenue administration and related records.
An office assistant who helps an officer to manage files, case papers, appointments and official correspondence.
An employee who prepares, records, files and processes office documents.
A support employee who carries files, delivers documents and performs basic office duties.
A place or department where official work is carried out OR in Revenue Department notified under Sindh Land Revenue, Act 1967.

Authorized Revenue Court as defined under Sindh Land Revenue Act 1967, where legal cases and disputes are heard and decided. other than Court of Law as defined in Constitution of Pakistan or intaact law/rules
A government or organisational unit responsible for a particular area of work.
An administrative area within a district, made up of several localities or revenue areas.
An administrative area of a province that contains several smaller areas, such as talukas.
A recognised revenue area used for land records and revenue administration.
An area of ground, whether used for farming, buildings or another purpose.
Land mainly used for growing crops or other farming activities.
A piece of land intended for building or using a home.
The legal right to possess, use and control property.
A person or organisation that legally owns something.
The actual holding, occupation or control of property, which may be different from legal ownership.
A person who uses or occupies property belonging to someone else, usually in return for rent.
An arrangement that allows someone to use property for an agreed period, usually in return for payment.
A number assigned to a land parcel so it can be identified in survey and land records.
The process of measuring the size and dimensions of a piece of land. In Revenue department, Sindh, also known as "Demarcation"
The line that marks where one piece of land ends and another begins.
The process of identifying and marking the exact boundaries of a piece of land.
Unauthorised occupation or use of land belonging to another person or the government.
An official land record showing recorded owners or holders and the rights associated with land.
An update made in official land records when ownership or another recorded land right changes.
An official copy or extract of information from the land record, often showing ownership details.
Property or rights received by a person after someone dies.
A person who is legally entitled to receive property from someone who has died.
A court-issued document that identifies a person's entitlement to collect certain debts or securities of someone who has died.
A legal document recording the sale and transfer of property from a seller to a buyer.
A legal document recording the voluntary transfer of property from one person to another without payment.
A legal document authorising another person to act on someone's behalf for specified matters.
The division of jointly owned property into separate shares or portions.
A government charge or tax imposed on land owner under the applicable revenue laws.
A charge for water supplied for irrigating agricultural land.
Money or another benefit given to someone for a loss, damage or property taken for public use also known as in Official Language as "Land Acquisition"
A formal request made to an office or authority for action or a service.
A document with questions or fields that a person completes to make a formal request.
A written statement of facts that a person formally swears or affirms is true.
Special paper on which certain legal documents are prepared, with the required stamp duty paid.
An official document confirming a fact, status, qualification or entitlement.
An official document showing the district or area a person is recognised as belonging to for legal or administrative purposes.
An official document confirming that an authority has no objection to a proposed action.
The Computerised National Identity Card issued in Pakistan as proof of a person's identity.
A copy confirmed by an authorised person as matching the original document.
The first or authentic version of a document, rather than a copy.
A paper copy made from an original document using a photocopier or scanner.
A person's handwritten name or mark used to confirm or approve a document.
A print of a person's thumb used to identify them or confirm a document when required.
An official mark placed on a document to show its source, approval or authenticity.
A document or record confirming that money or an item has been received.
A payment form or slip used to deposit a government fee, tax or other amount.
An official summon informing a person about something they must know or do or to appear before Revenue Officer authorized.
An official instruction or decision issued by an authorised officer or authority.
An official written announcement that communicates a government decision, rule, appointment or instruction.
A written message sent formally from one person or office to another.
A written account of information, facts, activities or findings.
A book or electronic record used to enter and organise official information.
Information kept in written, printed or electronic form as evidence or for future reference.
A collection of related documents kept together for official work or reference.
Money paid for a service, application or official process.
A formal meeting where an officer or court listens to the parties in a matter.
The scheduled date on which a case or matter is to be heard.
The postponement of a hearing or meeting to another date or time.
An official order requiring a person to appear before a court or authorised officer.
A statement that reports a problem, unfair treatment or alleged wrongdoing to an authority.
A formal written request asking an authority or court to take action or provide relief.
A request asking a higher authority or court to review a decision.
A conclusion or choice made by an authorised person or body after considering a matter.
An order that temporarily stops a particular action or proceeding until further direction or decision.
A person who saw an event or knows relevant facts and may provide information about them.
A spoken or written account of facts or information given by a person.
Information, documents or objects used to support or challenge a claim.
An official process of asking questions and examining facts about a matter.
The process of checking whether information or documents are correct and genuine.
A careful examination of a place, document, property or activity to check its condition or details.
A formal expression of disagreement or a reason why a request or action should not be accepted.
A disagreement between people or parties, for example about land, ownership or rights.
A person who submits an application or formal request.
A person who comes to an office to seek information, assistance or a service.
A numbered slip or marker used to manage the order in which people are served.
A line of people waiting for their turn.
A service desk where staff receive applications, documents or questions from the public.
A designated place where visitors sit or stand until they are called or assisted.
Information or advice that helps someone understand what to do or how to complete a process.
The established steps that must be followed to complete a task or official process.
Something that must be provided or completed before a request can be processed.
Official permission or acceptance given by an authorised person or authority.
Not yet completed or decided; still awaiting action.
Currently being examined or handled by the relevant office.
An official announcement intended to inform members of the public.
Official consent allowing a person to do something.
The duty to keep private or sensitive information from being shared without authorisation.
Government of Sindh.
